title: P keeps connect_pins' automatic 'Net-(ref-pin)' label, so every net it connects counts as named and P refuses the next legitimate join
verifier_method: Own geometry in pr57pt/verify-probe-decisions/v01_autolabel.py (.out). R1:1 and R2:1 sit in a row, R5:1 is on SIG, and R3/R4 are rotated 180 so every route is a clean straight wire. W1, W2 and W3 ran on P, M and B. Truth step: after P.connect, raw labels 'SIG' and 'AAA' on R1:1's end, judged by kicad-cli 9.0.8 (nets_coded + diff).

title: P reports 'already on N' or 'already connected' for joins KiCad never makes (label stacked with an NC flag, label on a pin end lying on a wire, bus-entry ends)
verifier_method: pr57pt/verify-probe-decisions/v06_false_noop.py (.out), own geometry. 6a: label N plus NC flag on a wire interior. 6b: label N on a pin end lying on the wire interior. 6c: wire to a bus entry's bus-side end. 6d: two entries sharing a point, no bus. 6e-LR and 6e-RL: junction on an unsplit wire. 6f: labels N and M stacked. Truth: raw label N on R1:1. Calls on P, M and B: wire N, wire Z, connect(R1:1,R5:1). Source re-read: 9.0.8 sch_label.cpp:1080-1180, 10.0.6 sch_label.cpp:1248-1290, 9.0.8 connection_graph.cpp:1345-1361, 9.0.8 sch_bus_entry.cpp:597-599, 10.0 connection_graph.cpp:1504-1518, 10.0 sch_bus_entry.cpp:580-582.

title: Literal M decides no-ops on its over-approximate model, so it repeats P's false no-ops for bus-entry and unsplit-junction geometry
verifier_method: pr57pt/verify-probe-decisions/v07_literal_M.py (.out). A literal-M emulator on mine_impl's item tables using M 5.2's own rules: every item at a point joins; two-ended items join their ends; label attach follows the K9 and K10 rules unioned (blocked only by a pin end or NC flag at the anchor); junction and entry ends join a line's interior; overlaps join; pad copies join. Decisions follow 5.4 step 2 and 5.5 step 2. Run on rebuilt 6a to 6e with the truth re-measured per fixture.

title: M's prototype refuses pins that every KiCad version reads as plainly unconnected, and its messages claim 'already on N'
verifier_method: pr57pt/verify-probe-decisions/v06_false_noop.py (M rows for 6a to 6d), v16_bus_bridge.py case c (wire end on a bare bus end), with attribution via v07_literal_M.py. Note: the 'literal M' column in v06 uses the prototype's capture rule; v07 is the authority for 6a and 6b.

title: P ignores the placed pin alternate when deciding power names, but KiCad uses it
verifier_method: pr57pt/verify-probe-decisions/v15_alternates.py (.out). Own lib: VALTP is a hidden power_in VDD pin with its passive alternate selected; VALTW is a hidden passive VDD pin with its power_in alternate selected; VHP is a plain VDD member. Truths use raw labels; calls f to i ran on P, M and B. Source: 9.0.8 sch_pin.cpp:279-297 (GetType follows the alternate), :323-327 (IsGlobalPower uses GetType), :1621-1637 (global power name is the lib pin name).
